# Executive Summary

This report delivers a rigorous, reproducible statistical and predictive analysis of secondary student academic performance based on the UCI Machine Learning Repository Mathematics Course dataset (*Cortez & Silva, 2008*). The analytical workflow operationalizes the requirements set forth in the **Student Performance Analytics Product Requirements Document (PRD v1.0)**.

Key findings include:
1. **Academic Persistence**: Prior period grades ($G1$ and $G2$) exhibit dominant explanatory power over the final grade ($G3$). Period 2 grade ($G2$) alone shares a correlation of $r = 0.905$ ($p < 0.001$) with $G3$.
2. **Behavioral Dynamics**: In univariate testing, weekly study time shows a modest, non-statistically significant relationship with final grades ($F(3, 391) = 1.728, p = 0.161$; Kruskal-Wallis $H(3) = 7.579, p = 0.056$). When controlling for prior marks in multiple linear regression, study time does not independently elevate final marks ($\beta = -0.201, p = 0.130$).
3. **Institutional Support Association**: Extra educational support (`schoolsup`) is positively associated with being classified as at-risk (45.1% in supported students vs. 31.1% in non-supported; Odds Ratio = 1.819, Fisher's exact $p = 0.055$). **Crucially, this association is non-causal** and reflects compensatory targeting (remedial assignment of struggling students).
4. **Mid-Course Predictive Utility**:
   - **Multiple Linear Regression**: Predicts final grade with a held-out test RMSE of **1.920** points and an $R^2$ of **0.8258**.
   - **Logistic Regression**: Classifies at-risk students ($G3 < 10$) on the held-out test set with **91.1% Accuracy**, **88.5% Sensitivity**, **92.5% Specificity**, and an **AUC of 0.980**.

# 1. Dataset Provenance & Preparation

```{r data_prep}
# Load dataset
df_raw <- read.csv("student-mat.csv", sep = ";", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df <- df_raw

# Factor encoding
cat_vars <- c("school", "sex", "address", "famsize", "Pstatus", "Mjob", "Fjob", 
              "reason", "guardian", "schoolsup", "famsup", "paid", "activities", 
              "nursery", "higher", "internet", "romantic")
df[cat_vars] <- lapply(df[cat_vars], as.factor)

df$studytime_num  <- df$studytime
df$studytime_fact <- factor(df$studytime, levels = 1:4, 
                            labels = c("<2 hrs", "2-5 hrs", "5-10 hrs", ">10 hrs"))

# Outcome definition
df$at_risk <- factor(ifelse(df$G3 < 10, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))

# Verification
cat(sprintf("Rows: %d | Columns: %d | Missing: %d | Duplicates: %d\n", 
            nrow(df), ncol(df), sum(is.na(df)), sum(duplicated(df))))
```

# 2. Exploratory Data Analysis & Visualizations

```{r viz_g3, fig.cap="Figure 1: Distribution of Final Grade (G3)"}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = G3)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 1, fill = "#2b5c8f", color = "white") +
  geom_density(color = "#d95f02", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 10, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Final Mathematics Grade Distribution (G3)", x = "Grade (0-20)", y = "Density")
```

```{r viz_studytime, fig.cap="Figure 2: Final Grade across Study Time Tiers"}
ggplot(df, aes(x = studytime_fact, y = G3, fill = studytime_fact)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Final Grade by Weekly Study Time", x = "Study Time", y = "Grade G3") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r viz_g2_g3, fig.cap="Figure 3: Second Period Grade versus Final Grade"}
ggplot(df, aes(x = G2, y = G3)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "#2b5c8f") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#d95f02", se = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Second Period Grade (G2) vs Final Grade (G3)", x = "Grade G2", y = "Grade G3")
```

# 3. Statistical Hypothesis Testing

## 3.1 Bivariate Grade Correlation
```{r corr_test}
cor.test(df$G2, df$G3, method = "pearson")
cor.test(df$G2, df$G3, method = "spearman")
```

## 3.2 Grade Differences across Study Time (ANOVA & Kruskal-Wallis)
```{r anova_test}
aov_fit <- aov(G3 ~ studytime_fact, data = df)
summary(aov_fit)
shapiro.test(residuals(aov_fit))
kruskal.test(G3 ~ studytime_fact, data = df)
```

## 3.3 Institutional Support vs. At-Risk Status
```{r chisq_test}
tbl <- table(df$schoolsup, df$at_risk)
chisq.test(tbl, correct = TRUE)
fisher.test(tbl)
```

---

# 4. Predictive Modeling & Holdout Evaluation

```{r modeling}
# Seeded Stratified Train/Test Split (80/20)
set.seed(42)
if (requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE)) {
  train_idx <- caret::createDataPartition(df$at_risk, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)
} else {
  train_idx <- sample(1:nrow(df), size = round(0.80 * nrow(df)))
}
train_data <- df[train_idx, ]
test_data  <- df[-train_idx, ]

# Linear Model
lm_model <- lm(G3 ~ G1 + G2 + studytime_num + absences + failures, data = train_data)
summary(lm_model)

# Test Linear Evaluation
test_pred_lm <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_data)
rmse <- sqrt(mean((test_data$G3 - test_pred_lm)^2))
mae  <- mean(abs(test_data$G3 - test_pred_lm))
cat(sprintf("Held-Out Linear Model -> RMSE: %.4f | MAE: %.4f\n", rmse, mae))

# Logistic Model
logit_model <- glm(at_risk ~ G1 + G2 + studytime_num + absences + failures + schoolsup, 
                   data = train_data, family = binomial)
summary(logit_model)

# Test Logistic Evaluation
test_prob_logit <- predict(logit_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
test_pred_class <- factor(ifelse(test_prob_logit >= 0.50, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
table(Actual = test_data$at_risk, Predicted = test_pred_class)
```

---

# 5. Ethical Guidelines & Responsible Use

1. **Non-Causal Interpretation**: Observational models identify statistical correlation, never causation. 
2. **Supportive, Not Punitive Application**: Predictions serve strictly as decision support to allocate tutoring and guidance, never to track, exclude, or discipline students.
3. **Mid-Course Decision Timing**: Predictions rely on G1/G2; earlier screening must be calibrated against pre-course variables.
